notes.10: In general this question was poorly answered. Both the parts were soluble by routine methods, yet candidates did not apply them to the right vectors. In part (i) the unknown plane is parallel to OC, hence its normal is perpendicular to OC. The plane contains AB hence its normal is perpendicular to AB. Thus, there is a choice of methods based on (a) a pair of zero scalar products of the unknown normal with ABand with OC, (b) the vector product of AB and OC, or (c) a two parameter equation involving the vectors AB, OC and the position vector of a point on AB, e.g. OA. Yet many candidates did not grasp the geometry of the situation and worked with irrelevant pairs of direction vectors such as AB and AC, or OA and OB. A similar situation arose in part (ii), though on the whole candidates did better in this section. There was a considerable variety of approaches. The most popular method was to take a general point P on AB with parameter Î» say, equate the scalar product CP.AB to zero, solve for Î» and calculate CP . Here again candidates applied the method to wrong pairs of vectors, e.g. CP and OC, or OP and AB. Answers: (i) 3x + z = 13; (ii) 3 2 .
